passages.context: The whole of Mishnah Berakhot 8:3, read in the retrieved response with the other seven mishnayot of the chapter in view so that the ruling's place in a list of Shammai and Hillel disputes about the meal is explicit. Registered as the only ancient rabbinic ruling about a cloth used at table.
passages.notes: Hebrew script with Torat Emet vowel pointing. Consuming publications that carry no Hebrew face transliterate this ruling and label the transliteration as such. In transliteration it reads: Beth Shammai omerim, meqanne'ah yadav ba-mappah u-mannihah al ha-shulhan. U-Veth Hillel omerim, al ha-keseth.

work.author: Rabbinic sages (tannaitic redaction)
work.description: The opening tractate of the Mishnah, on the recitation of the Shema, the Amidah, and blessings, including in chapter 8 a list of disputes between the House of Shammai and the House of Hillel about the conduct of a meal. The third of those disputes, at 8:3, is the only ancient rabbinic ruling about a cloth used at table: it concerns where a damp hand-towel may be laid so that it does not transmit ritual impurity. A locus is chapter.mishnah.
work.title: Mishnah Berakhot
